hypothesis: The settle-daemoninit3 lane's exact-bytes discriminator (bench record 20261001-175500) proved a REAL +68.6ms p50 submit_to_settle regression across the 25 commits e75f59efc6..b1c6b7a0c (e75 p50 711.0 vs b1c6 779.6, complete separation, paired same-VM, p=0.000155). The drift-bisect question: WHICH commit(s) introduce it. Pre-registered protocol: midpoint legs over the range's 18 product commits (P1..P18; P0=e75 the exact-bytes GOOD anchor; P18=b1c6b7a0c the BAD endpoint; the first midpoint P9=1ff9d86 splitting the product commits 9/9), each leg = an arm built on the SAME VM at the mid commit through the release pipeline and staged as its own sha-pinned bench product, then a 2-block ABBA (M,e,e,M) vs the e75 anchor with pi control rounds pre/post; pre-registered verdict bands: all per-block paired deltas < +25ms GOOD, all > +45ms BAD, else PARTIAL-splits-both.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY (no product change). Same VM as the discriminator (hillclimb-perf-settlehold sandbox u5nxl6eddrafmr7cbe1viyui, ubuntu:22.04, 16c/32GB, rustup 1.98.1, bench harness /root/bench-harness, mock-routed compare.msg_send, PTY 120x40, per-trial fresh launch). This successor lane re-collected the predecessor's inert session first: its P9 arm build had DIED at assemble_artifacts (the build-arm.sh assemble call was missing the --decoder argument) and NO bisect legs had run; the fixed script (local + VM copies in sync) re-staged rust-1ff9d86 with BINSHA c822c64974431c4e25a1e2c67fe6c2e0492be312ff5bb95d57d869245c5066f2 (56058440 bytes) BYTE-IDENTICAL to the sha the predecessor's own split_debug had recorded at 18:23Z before the break. Each bisect arm: cargo build --release --locked at the pinned commit -> split_debug.py shipped ELF + decoder -> assemble_artifacts.py release tarball -> staged at /root/bench-lane/<arm>/ -> registered as its own bench product with binary_sha256 pinned in product.yaml and re-asserted by every leg round's versions.json; warm-arm (settle walk + warm_kernels + own-daemon kernel venv + launch-verify import rlm.repl) before each leg; leg-abba driver: zombie sweep before timing, I/O advisory v1.0 regime probe at BOTH boundaries, spin calibration pre/mid/post, pi control rounds pre/post, per-round noop PTY floor. Legs run quiet-gated (no build while a leg times). VERDICTS: P9 BAD -> P5 BAD -> P3 BAD -> P2 PARTIAL -> P1 BAD (the chain ran the deciding legs on the BAD side of each split).
parity_notes: No product bytes changed anywhere; every arm is a measurement arm built from upstream commits as-is. The e75 anchor is the r2 campaign pin's exact payload staged verbatim (binary_sha256 0ba7c9b6e6277b6301605769240d133727d59dc1997890e333e54518ce5a88e5) and the pi control is byte-identical to the r2 campaign's pi arm (0.99.1@d86654ab, cli.js e79626f2) — the cross-campaign control. Bisect arms' kernel venvs were bootstrapped by each arm's own daemon; the settle metric is kernel-venv-insensitive (the predecessor disclosed this; the turn completes without kernel interaction). Tooling defects disclosed: (1) analyze-leg.py's phase-string grouping misses the pi control rows (phase bisect-<tag>-prepi-pi parses round/tag-role differently) — the pi values in this record are read directly from the trials jsonl, NOT from the analyzer; (2) the lane's collect-summary.json keys noop/versions by round name, and the 4 e75 round names repeat per leg (b1e1-rust-e75 etc.) so the summary snapshot holds one of each — the per-round files for ALL 50 rounds are the ground truth in the evidence archive.

outcome: measured - THE SETTLE-DRIFT BISECT CONVERGED IN THE TIMEBOX: the +68.6ms submit_to_settle regression is INTRODUCED AT 603376a (#3188 make forked sessions fully isolated), the FIRST commit after the GOOD e75 anchor — P1 measured BAD directly (+146.3/+82.9 block deltas, pooled p50 +142.0ms, e75 anchor p50 670.3 in the same leg), so no interpolation is needed: the window e75..603376a contains exactly one commit and it is BAD. Every later midpoint contains P1 and measures BAD/PARTIAL as expected (P2 PARTIAL +79.5/+37.2, P3 BAD +67.4/+75.1, P5 BAD +95.9/+69.0, P9 BAD +105.4/+93.4; endpoint P18 +68.6).
decision: THE VERDICT: the settle regression the settle-hold lane found is #3188's introduction — the fork-isolation family's supervisor-side identity machinery (sync_root_identity_from_roster re-binding the descriptor + persisted record + durable create command + binding table onto roster rows; the boot reconcile-from-live-state before routing opens; the unreconciled-boot quarantine fencing every route; the owned-session scan fenced by the quarantine — 11 bullets, all #3188-family). MECHANISM HYPOTHESIS (unproven, the follow-up's first target): the per-trial fresh-launch msg_send turn now pays the #3188 boot-path work between launch and route-open (reconcile + quarantine-fenced owned-session scan), which sits directly on the submit_to_settle clock; the durable-persist side of the identity follow is the second candidate (a per-write sync on the DEGRADED fresh-fsync host). MAGNITUDE ACCOUNTING (honest): the per-leg pooled deltas are NOT monotonic (P1 +142 -> P2 +49 -> P3 +67 -> P5 +76 -> P9 +100 -> P18 +68.6) because (a) the host phase moved the e75 anchor p50 670-736 across legs, and (b) P2's batch carries settle-adjacent PERF PRs (the O(1) catalog-fold counter, 64KiB fold reads) that plausibly claw back a share of what P1 added — the verdict column is phase-independent (paired), the magnitude column is not; the per-commit magnitude table is the honest residual question. THE NEXT LANE: instrument the #3188 changes directly at P1 (bind-span/turn decompose on the 603376a arm vs e75 — reconcile cost, quarantine fence, scan, and the durable persist inside the identity follow), then the P1->P2 claw-back decompose to explain the magnitude non-monotonicity. NO PR (measurement-only; #3188 already merged upstream — the fix question is a product decision on the found regression, not this lane's).
